headline: Midwest mills open November scrap buying about $20 a ton higher
detail: Mills opened November trade with prime grade bids up about $20 a gross ton, a second monthly gain after October's roughly $30 rise. Chicago busheling and shred should settle higher.

headline: Jobs report for October lands at 7:30am today
detail: Forecasts call for about 55,000–65,000 jobs and 4.2% unemployment after September's weak 29,000. A strong number lifts December rate-hike bets and the dollar, which weighs on metals; a weak one helps gold and copper.

headline: Copper heads for its worst week since March as tech stocks slide
detail: LME copper slipped to about $13,760 a ton Friday, down about 2.8% for the week, as a selloff in AI-linked stocks hit sentiment. Tight supply outside the US and a record China import premium kept the drop from going further; expect softer copper scrap bids.

headline: Survey points to about 7% higher US scrap prices for November
detail: Fastmarkets' monthly survey signals roughly a 7% month-on-month rise, with strong mill order books, rising coil prices and thin scrap flows into yards. Supports a firmer Chicago settle next week.

headline: US quietly restarts tariff talks with Canada on steel, aluminum and autos
detail: Commerce Secretary Lutnick has reopened talks that stalled in August, when Canada reportedly had a steel quota and an aluminum tariff cut lined up. Any aluminum tariff cut would pull the Midwest premium lower.

headline: Nucor lifts its coil price for a 15th straight week
detail: Nucor's weekly hot-rolled coil price rose $10 to $1,280 a short ton, and the market is near a four-year high largely because of tariffs. Strong sheet prices keep mills hungry for prime scrap.

headline: Copper swings on the midterm results and doubts over a refined copper tariff
detail: LME copper fell to its lowest since early August after Democrats won Congress, then recovered, while COMEX rose to about $6.44. If the planned US tariff on refined copper is dropped, metal stockpiled in the US could flow out and squeeze the COMEX premium.

headline: Fed's Hammack backs frequent small rate hikes
detail: The Cleveland Fed president, who voted for a hike last week when the Fed held at 3.75–4.00%, says inflation is still too high. More hikes would mean a firmer dollar and a headwind for metals.

headline: LME aluminum jumps 1.7% as warehouse stocks keep falling
detail: Cash aluminum rose about $53 to roughly $3,135 a ton on Nov 4 as LME stocks slipped near 229,000 tons and more metal was booked for removal. A tight market supports aluminum scrap values.

headline: Gold climbs to a two-week high after the election as stocks plunge
detail: Gold touched about $4,148 Thursday and ended near $4,087 as the dollar and yields fell, while silver slipped below $52 on industrial selling. Odds of a December Fed hike dropped after the stock rout.

headline: October car sales pace drops to its slowest since January
detail: Cox Automotive put October sales at a 15.5 million annual pace, with weak retail buying and sales down about 1.5% for the year. Slower sales risk lower auto output and less factory scrap from stamping plants.

headline: China's factory activity slips back into contraction
detail: China's official manufacturing index fell to 49.3 in October, with new orders shrinking too. That is a weak sign for Chinese demand for copper, aluminum and steel.
source: National Bureau of Statistics of China

headline: Strike at Canada's biggest copper mine drags on with no talks set
detail: About 1,200 union workers at Teck's Highland Valley mine in British Columbia have been out since Oct 24 over pay and safety, with no bargaining scheduled. A long strike tightens an already short copper concentrate market.

headline: Canada's aluminum makers hope the Democratic win brings tariff relief
detail: The 50% US tariff has pushed about 800,000 tons of Canadian aluminum to Europe since March 2025, and the industry group is more hopeful now. Analysts don't expect a quick change, so the high Midwest premium likely stays for now.

headline: Stocks have their worst day since April 2025
detail: The S&P 500 fell about 4.4% and the Nasdaq about 5.5% Thursday, led by chip stocks. The risk-off mood dragged copper and silver lower but cut December rate-hike odds.

headline: Sibanye cuts its US palladium output forecast after a strike
detail: Sibanye-Stillwater lowered its 2026 Montana guidance to 245,000–255,000 ounces from 280,000–300,000 after a five-week strike; US output fell 19% in the third quarter. Less new palladium supports catalytic converter values.

headline: Nickel jumps about 7% this week on Indonesian quota talk
detail: LME nickel closed near $16,315 a ton Thursday after Indonesian officials backed controlling output through mine permits. That firms stainless and nickel-alloy scrap.

headline: Construction spending falls 1.9% in September as housing drops
detail: Total construction spending fell to a $2.19 trillion annual pace, with home building down 5.5% while private nonresidential rose 1.1%. Weak housing means less demand for rebar, wire and copper plumbing.

headline: Iron ore hits a one-month high on a Chinese stock rally
detail: Dalian iron ore rose about 1.6% and Singapore futures topped $92 as better Chinese steel margins raised hopes for more output. Shanghai coil and rebar also rose about 1%.

headline: Palladium and platinum bounce hard from oversold levels
detail: Palladium jumped about 8% and platinum about 5.6% on Nov 4, with palladium adding about 2% more Thursday. Both remain below their longer-term averages, so converter prices are still in a downtrend despite the bounce.

headline: Trump and Xi set to meet at APEC with the trade truce ending Jan 10
detail: The two leaders are expected to meet Nov 18–19 in Shenzhen, and analysts expect export controls to stay tight whoever runs Congress. The outcome affects tariffs and Chinese metal demand.

headline: Sales pace slips below 16 million as Toyota and Korean brands gain
detail: CarPro put October at a 15.6 million pace, with Toyota up 5.7% and Hyundai and Kia setting October records while Detroit brands lagged.

headline: Gold near $4,120 as the dollar weakens, but rate-hike bets cap gains
detail: The dollar had its weakest close since late September and oil fell sharply after the election, easing inflation worries. Gold is still well below its $5,608 record.

headline: Rio Tinto begins restarting Oyu Tolgoi underground mine after rockfall
detail: A rockfall at the Mongolian copper-gold mine on Oct 29 injured three workers; Rio is restarting step by step. Border trucking delays are also slowing concentrate shipments to China.

headline: Aluminum seen moving sideways next week
detail: SMM expects LME aluminum between about $2,950 and $3,090, with near 20-year-low stocks offset by weak Chinese processing demand and faster Middle East smelter restarts.

headline: US tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and autos stay after the midterms
detail: Section 232 rates of 25–50% still apply and no deal has been published; comments for the 2027 USMCA review are due Jan 12. No relief yet for cross-border metal flows.

headline: Silver rebounds from a one-year low but rate worries limit gains
detail: Silver bounced from about $48.60 on Nov 3 to above $53 Thursday before easing. An analyst warns hike bets and possible curbs on data-center spending could send it back toward $48.

headline: Mortgage rates ease to about 7% after the election
detail: The 30-year fixed rate dipped about 17 basis points in a week as Treasury yields fell. Rates near 7% still hold back home building.

headline: China's iron output dips less than expected
detail: Mysteel showed China's daily hot-metal output down only about 0.2% to about 2.32 million tons, keeping iron ore steady near $91 at the time.

headline: EV share stalls near 7% as hybrids carry auto sales
detail: EVs were 7.0% of October sales, down from a year ago, while hybrids surged. Slower EV uptake trims copper and aluminum battery demand.
